expectations.text: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
expectations.evidence: Assumptions A1-A7 and Open Questions Q1-Q6 plus a companion notes file.

expectations.text: Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Summary, Background, Goals, Non-Goals, Validation Rule Catalog (requirements), Acceptance Criteria, Testing Strategy, Open Questions.

expectations.text: Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
expectations.evidence: G1-G6, N1-N6, rule IDs TV-001..TV-407, AC1-AC11.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
expectations.evidence: AC1-AC11 specify exit codes, per-rule fixtures, JSON schema validation, and a read-only checksum check.

expectations.text: Mentions relevant existing workspace context, especially the ticket workflow skill or `.tickets` conventions, based on read-only inspection.
expectations.evidence: Only .gitignore was inspected; the agent explicitly did NOT read the ticket-workflow skill and invented a generic schema (statuses backlog/in-review/cancelled) that contradicts the real to-do/in-progress/done/blocked lifecycle. Grounding is superficial.

expectations.text: Does not create implementation code, ticket files, or unrelated documentation outside the assigned output directory.
expectations.evidence: Only the spec and notes file were written; explicit scope note that this is a specification only.

expectations.text: Functional requirements are written in EARS form, using 'shall' with When/If/While/Where keywords where appropriate.
expectations.evidence: Requirements are expressed as Goals ('Detect...', 'Enforce...') and a rule-catalog table of descriptions; no EARS 'shall' statements with When/If/While/Where.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria use Given/When/Then phrasing and reference the requirement IDs they verify (traceability).
expectations.evidence: AC1-AC11 are prose pass/fail bullets ('A fully valid ticket set produces 0 errors...'); no Given/When/Then and no (verifies REQ-###) mapping.

expectations.text: Includes a 'For Implementing Agents' handoff orientation that identifies authoritative sections and treats open questions as blockers rather than guessing.
expectations.evidence: No 'For Implementing Agents' section; no statement that open questions are blockers.

uncertainties: Baseline intentionally avoided skill files, so the ticket schema is hypothetical and partly wrong.
workarounds: Made schema config-driven to absorb the wrong assumptions later.
